'''George William Foster''' (born October 7, 1955) is an American businessman, physicist, and politician serving as the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]] for {{ushr|Illinois|11}} since 2013.<ref name=cbs-6-11-2012>{{cite web|title=Judy Biggert Concedes Race To Bill Foster|publisher=[[WBBM-TV]] |date=November 6, 2012|url=http://chicago.cbslocal.com/2012/11/06/biggert-concedes-race-to-foster/|access-date=November 8, 2012|archive-date=November 10, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110105011/http://chicago.cbslocal.com/2012/11/06/biggert-concedes-race-to-foster/|url-status=live}}</ref> He was the U.S. representative for {{ushr|Illinois|14}} from 2008 to 2011. He is a member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]].

==Early life and education==
Foster was born in 1955 in [[Madison, Wisconsin]]. As a teenager, he attended [[James Madison Memorial High School]]. He received his [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[physics]] from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1976 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in physics from [[Harvard University]] in 1983.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/bill-foster/gIQAnjxyDP_print.html|title=Bill Foster - Who Runs Government|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=August 10, 2018|archive-date=August 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810145056/https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/bill-foster/gIQAnjxyDP_print.html?noredirect=on|url-status=dead}}</ref> The title of his doctoral dissertation is "An experimental limit on proton decay: <math>p \rightarrow \mathrm{positron} + \pi^0</math>."<ref>{{cite book |last1=Foster |first1=George William |title=A Experimental Limit on Proton Decay: Proton ---&gt; Positron + Neutral Pion |date=1983 |publisher=Harvard University |bibcode=1983PhDT........48F |language=en }}</ref>

When Foster was 19, he started a company with his younger brother, Fred. The company, [[Electronic Theatre Controls]], has become a manufacturer of theatrical lighting fixtures and control systems.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.billfoster.com/meet-bill/bills-family/| title=Bill's Business Career |website=Bill Foster for Congress |language=en-US |access-date=February 4, 2024}}</ref>

==Physics career==
After completing his Ph.D., Foster moved to the [[Fox Valley (Illinois)|Fox Valley]] with his family to pursue a career in [[Particle physics|high-energy (particle) physics]] at [[Fermilab]], a [[United States Department of Energy National Laboratories|Department of Energy National Laboratory]]. During his 22 years at Fermilab, he participated in several projects, including the design of equipment and data analysis software for the [[Collider Detector at Fermilab|CDF Detector]], which were used in the discovery of the [[top quark]], and the management of the design and construction of a 3&nbsp;km Anti-Proton Recycler Ring for the Main Injector.<ref>{{cite web|last=Foster|first=G. William|title=[4C.01] The Fermilab Permanent Magnet Antiproton Recycler Ring|work=The 1997 Particle Accelerator Conference Meeting Program Vancouver BC, Canada|publisher=Fermilab|date=May 12–16, 1997|url=http://flux.aps.org/meetings/YR97/BAPSPAC97/abs/S240001.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030718115424/http://flux.aps.org/meetings/YR97/BAPSPAC97/abs/S240001.html|archive-date=July 18, 2003|url-status=live|access-date=February 24, 2008|df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/2006/0501/p02s01-stss.html |title=Physicists hope to win support for new subatomic smasher |author=Spotts, Peter N. |newspaper=The Christian Science Monitor |date=2004-05-01 |access-date=2008-03-11 |archive-date=2008-09-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905233314/http://www.csmonitor.com/2006/0501/p02s01-stss.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 1998, Foster was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1998&unit_id=&institution=Fermi+National+Accelerator+Laboratory}} (search on year=1998 and institution=Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory)</ref> He was a member of the team that received the 1989 [[Bruno Rossi Prize]] for [[cosmic ray]] physics for the discovery of the [[neutrino]] burst from the [[supernova]] [[SN 1987A]]. He also received the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]]' Particle Accelerator Technology Prize and was awarded an Energy Conservation award from the [[United States Department of Energy]] for his application of permanent magnets for [[Fermilab]]'s [[Particle accelerator|accelerators]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aas.org/head/rossi/rossi.recip.html#E |title=HEAD AAS Rossi Prize Winners |author=American Astronomical Society – High Energy Astrophysics Division |year=1989 |access-date=2008-03-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080406082614/http://www.aas.org/head/rossi/rossi.recip.html |archive-date=April 6, 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He and Stephen D. Holmes received the [[Robert R. Wilson Prize|Robert R. Wilson Prize for Achievement in the Physics of Particle Accelerators]] in 2022 for "leadership in developing the modern accelerator complex at Fermilab, enabling the success of the Tevatron program that supports rich programs in neutrino and precision physics."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prize Recipient |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm |access-date=2023-01-23 |publisher=American Physical Society |language=en}}</ref>

==U.S. House of Representatives==

===Elections===
;2008 special
{{Main|2008 Illinois's 14th congressional district special election}}

On November 26, 2007, former House Republican Speaker [[Dennis Hastert|J. Dennis Hastert]] resigned as the Representative from Illinois's 14th congressional district. Foster announced his candidacy to fill the vacancy on May 30, 2007.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://docs.newsbank.com/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info:sid/iw.newsbank.com:NewsBank:ECNB&rft_val_format=info:ofi/fmt:kev:mtx:ctx&rft_dat=119D38CBB4CC8A60&svc_dat=InfoWeb:aggregated5&req_dat=AA98CDC331574F0ABEAFF732B33DC0B2 |title=Geneva man seeks position in Congress |publisher=Courier News (Elgin, IL) |date=2007-05-31 |access-date=2008-03-11 |archive-date=2016-01-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160120222436/http://docs.newsbank.com/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info%3Asid%2Fiw.newsbank.com%3ANewsBank%3AECNB&rft_val_format=info%3Aofi%2Ffmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Actx&rft_dat=119D38CBB4CC8A60&svc_dat=InfoWeb%3Aaggregated5&req_dat=AA98CDC331574F0ABEAFF732B33DC0B2 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the March special election, Foster defeated Republican nominee and Hastert-endorsed candidate [[Jim Oberweis]], 53%–47%.<ref name="General Election">{{cite news |url=http://hosted.ap.org/dynamic/files/elections/2008/by_county/IL_Page_0308.html?SITE=ILCHTELN&SECTION=POLITICS |title=General election results |date=2008-03-08 |newspaper=Chicago Tribune |access-date=2008-03-12 |archive-date=2008-03-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080312123056/http://hosted.ap.org/dynamic/files/elections/2008/by_county/IL_Page_0308.html?SITE=ILCHTELN&SECTION=POLITICS |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=IL – District 14 – Special Election|work=Our Campaigns|url=http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=403895|access-date=2012-03-21|archive-date=2014-10-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141026123244/http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=403895|url-status=live}}</ref>

;2008 general
{{Main|2008 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 14}}

In November, Oberweis ran against Foster again. Foster won reelection to a full term, 58%–42%.<ref>{{cite web|title=IL – District 14|work=Our Campaigns|url=http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=343142|access-date=2012-03-21|archive-date=2011-06-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615052959/http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=343142|url-status=live}}</ref>

;2010
{{Main|2010 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 14}}

Foster was challenged by Republican nominee State Senator [[Randy Hultgren]] and Green Party nominee Daniel Kairis. |newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=2010-10-07 |access-date=2010-10-09 }}</ref> the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]''<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.suntimes.com/news/elections/endorsements/2775994,CST-EDT-edit06a.article |title=Foster for 14th District |newspaper=[[Chicago web|url=http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=489038|title=Our Campaigns – IL – District 14 Race – Nov 02, 2010|work=Our Campaigns |access-date=September 7, 2015|archive-date=January 20, ;2012
{{Main|2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 11}}

In May 2011, Foster sold his home in [[Geneva, Illinois|Geneva]], moved to [[Naperville, Illinois|Naperville]] and announced plans to run for Congress in the 11th district, which encompasses [[Aurora, Illinois|Aurora]], [[Joliet, Illinois|Joliet]], [[Lisle, Illinois|Lisle]] in addition to Naperville. It also includes roughly a quarter of his former district.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/sweet/2011/05/illinois_congress_2012_bill_fo_1.html |title=Illinois Congress 2012: Bill Foster running in new 11th district |author=Lynn Sweet |date=31 May 2011 |work=Chicago Sun Times |access-date=June 1, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110602011613/http://blogs.suntimes.com/sweet/2011/05/illinois_congress_2012_bill_fo_1.html |archive-date=June 2, 2011 }}</ref><ref name="chitribmay">{{cite news |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/news/local/breaking/chibrknews-in-wake-of-remap-plan-exlawmaker-to-run-again-20110531,0,1494745.story |title=In wake of remap plan, ex-lawmaker to run again |author=Katherine Skiba |date=31 May 2011 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=June 1, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026090343/http://www.chicagotribune.com/news/local/breaking/chibrknews-in-wake-of-remap-plan-exlawmaker-to-run-again-20110531,0,1494745.story |archive-date=26 October 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The district had previously been the 13th, represented by seven-term Republican [[Judy Biggert]]. Although Biggert's home in [[Hinsdale, Illinois|Hinsdale]] had been shifted to the Chicago-based 5th district, Biggert opted to seek election in the 11th, which contained half of her old territory.<ref>{{cite web|last=Mike Flannery|first=Dane Placko|title=FOX Chicago Sunday: Biggert, Foster debate to represent 11th Congressional District
|publisher=[[WFLD]]|date=Aug 9, 2012|url=http://www.myfoxchicago.com/story/19238594/judy-biggert-bill-foster-debate-cadidates-congressional-district-11-fox-chicago-sunday|url-status=dead
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121126094540/http://www.myfoxchicago.com/story/19238594/judy-biggert-bill-foster-debate-cadidates-congressional-district-11-fox-chicago-sunday
|archive-date=2012-11-26}}</ref>
[[File:Bill Foster, Official Portrait, 113th Congress (3x4).jpg|thumb|right|Foster in 2013]]
On November 6, 2012, Foster won the election for the 11th district with 58% of the vote.<ref>{{cite news|last=Matt Hanley|first=Jenette Sturges|title=Foster returns to Congress with win over Biggert|work=The Herald-News|date=November 6, 2012|url=http://heraldnews.suntimes.com/news/elections/16065869-418/foster-returns-to-congress-with-win-over-biggert.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130203052511/http://heraldnews.suntimes.com/news/elections/16065869-418/foster-returns-to-congress-with-win-over-biggert.html|url-status=dead
|archive-date=February 3, 2013}}</ref>

;
;2014
{{Main|2014 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 11}}

Foster ran again and was unopposed in the Democratic primary.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elections.il.gov/Downloads/ElectionInformation/VoteTotals/2014GPOfficialVote.pdf|title=Official Illinois State Board of Elections Results – March 18, 2014 Primary Election (P. 31)|access-date=December 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021140211/http://www.elections.il.gov/Downloads/ElectionInformation/VoteTotals/2014GPOfficialVote.pdf|archive-date=October 21, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the general election, he defeated the Republican nominee, State Representative [[Darlene Senger]], with 53.5% of the vote to her 46.5%.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionInformation/GetVoteTotals.aspx|title=Illinois General Election 2014|publisher=Illinois State Board of Elections|date=2014-11-04|access-date=2014-12-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215214831/http://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionInformation/GetVoteTotals.aspx|archive-date=2014-12-15|url-status=dead}}</ref>

;2016
{{Main|2016 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 11}}

Foster ran again and was unopposed in the Democratic primary.<ref name=Foster_Ballotpedia>{{cite web|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Bill_Foster_(Illinois)|access-date=March 22, 2022|title=Bill Foster (Illinois) }}</ref> In the general election, he defeated the Republican nominee, Tonia Khouri, with 60.4% of the vote to her 39.6%.<ref name=Foster_Ballotpedia/>

;2018
{{Main|2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 11}}

Foster again was unopposed in the Democratic primary. In the general election, he defeated the Republican nominee, Nick Stella, with 63.8% of the vote to Stella's 36.2%.<ref name=Foster_Ballotpedia/>

;2020
{{Main|2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 11}}

Foster faced a primary challenge from Rachel Ventura and won the nomination with 58.7% of the vote. In the general election, he defeated Republican nominee, Rick Laib, with 63.3% of the vote.<ref name=Foster_Ballotpedia/>

'''2022'''

{{Main|2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 11}}

Foster won the June 28 Democratic primary.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bill Foster (Illinois) |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Bill_Foster_(Illinois) |access-date=2022-09-12 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}</ref> In the general election, he defeated Catalina Lauf with 56.45% of the vote.

===Tenure===
Although it was initially thought that Foster would not be sworn in until April 2008 due to the need to count absentee ballots before his first election was certified, he took the oath of office on March 11, 2008.<ref name="hague_20080311">{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyherald.com/story/?id=151577&src=5 |newspaper=Daily Herald |title=Foster sworn into Congress |date=2008-03-11 |access-date=2008-03-12 |author=Hague, Leslie |archive-date=2008-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080918165307/http://www.dailyherald.com/story/?id=151577&src=5 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Foster joined [[Vern Ehlers]] and [[Rush D. Holt Jr.|Rush Holt Jr.]] as the only [[physicist|research physicists]] ever elected to Congress.<ref>{{cite news|author=Cornelia Dean|title=Physicists in Congress Calculate Their Influence|date=2008-07-10|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/06/10/science/10phys.html|access-date=2010-02-11|archive-date=2013-08-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130813080902/http://www.nytimes.com/2008/06/10/science/10phys.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On his first day in office, he cast the deciding vote to keep from [[Table (parliamentary)|tabling]] an ethics bill that would create an independent outside panel to investigate ethics complaints against House members.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2008/roll121.xml |title=Final Vote Results for Roll Call 121 |date=2008-03-11 |access-date=2008-03-13 |archive-date=2008-03-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080327010415/http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2008/roll121.xml |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/news/politics/blog/2008/03/first_day_swing_vote_for_new_r.html|title=First day, swing vote for new Rep. Bill Foster|author=Jim Tankersley|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080317122525/http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/news/politics/blog/2008/03/first_day_swing_vote_for_new_r.html|archive-date=2008-03-17}}</ref>

;Fundraising
According to [[OpenSecrets]], Foster received $637,050 from labor-related political action committees during his runs for Congress. $180,000 of this money came from [[Political action committee|PACs]] linked to public sector unions. $110,000 of these donations came from PACs linked to industrial labor unions.

According to the [[Federal Election Commission]], [[Nancy Pelosi]] gave $4,000 to Foster's 2012 campaign committee. PACs under Pelosi's control donated $10,000 to his 2012 campaign.

== Political positions ==
Foster voted with President Joe Biden's stated position 100% of the time in the [[117th United States Congress|117th Congress]], according to a ''[[FiveThirtyEight]]'' analysis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bycoffe |first=Aaron |last2=Wiederkehr |first2=Anna |date=2021-04-22 |title=Does Your Member Of Congress Vote With Or Against Biden? |url=https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/biden-congress-votes/house/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423141050/https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/biden-congress-votes/house/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 23, 2021 |access-date=2023-11-15 |website=FiveThirtyEight |language=en}}</ref>

=== Taxes ===
Foster supported allowing the [[Bush tax cuts]] to expire. During a debate with his opponent in the 2012 election, Foster said, "The tax cuts were promised to generate job growth, but did not. If you follow the money, when you give a dollar to a very wealthy person, they won't typically put it back into the local economy." He said the tax benefits ended up in overseas accounts and spent on luxury purchases.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dauskurdas|first=Sherri|title=Biggert, Foster sit down for first debate of new 11th district|work=The Bugle|date=September 2, 2012|url=http://www.buglenewspapers.com/joliet/article_05bd8cd6-f51f-11e1-a3ff-001a4bcf6878.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910050602/http://www.buglenewspapers.com/joliet/article_05bd8cd6-f51f-11e1-a3ff-001a4bcf6878.html|archive-date=2012-09-10}}</ref>

Foster has opposed efforts to repeal the estate tax. On August 31, 2005, U.S. Newswire reported that Foster said, "The proponents of estate tax repeal are fond of calling it the 'death tax'. It's not a death tax, it's a Rich Kids' tax." In 2009, just before the estate tax was scheduled for a one-year repeal, Foster voted to permanently extend the then current estate tax rate of 45%.

=== Card check ===
According to the official Thomas website, Foster co-sponsored the [[Employee Free Choice Act]] of 2009, which would enable unionization of small businesses of less than 50 employees. On February 25, 2012, the ''Daily Herald'' reported, "Foster pointed to his support for the Employee Free Choice Act while serving at the congressman in the 14th District as proof of his union support."

=== Stimulus spending ===
Foster voted for the [[American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=FINAL VOTE RESULTS FOR ROLL CALL 46 |url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2009/roll046.xml |website=house.gov |access-date=2012-04-13 |archive-date=2017-07-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170705062157/http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2009/roll046.xml |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Health care reform ===
Foster voted for the [[Affordable Care Act]] (Obamacare).<ref>{{cite web|title=Final Vote Results for Roll Call 165|work=HR 3590 Recorded Vote : Bill Title: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act|publisher=U.S. House of Representatives|date=21 Mar 2010|url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2010/roll165.xml|access-date=April 13, 2012|archive-date=February 5, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110205004628/http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2010/roll165.xml|url-status=live}}</ref> On June 29, 2012, the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' reported that Foster said of his vote for Obamacare, "I'm proud of my vote, and I would be proud to do it again."

=== Dodd-Frank ===
He also voted for the [[Dodd–Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act]], with all 10 of the amendments he proposed being added to the final bill.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bill's Congressional Career|work=Billfoster.com|publisher=Bill Foster for Congress|url=http://www.billfoster.com/about/congress/|access-date=2012-04-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325065559/http://www.billfoster.com/about/congress/|archive-date=2012-03-25|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Environment ===
He voted against the [[American Clean Energy and Security Act]], which would create a [[Cap and trade]] system.<ref>{{cite web|title=Final Vote Results for Roll Call 477: HR 2454|work=Recorded Vote; Question: On Passage; Bill Title: American Clean Energy and Security Act|publisher=U.S. House of Representatives|date=26 Jun 2009|url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2009/roll477.xml|access-date=April 13, 2012|archive-date=3 February 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110203083736/http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2009/roll477.xml|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Second Amendment ===
Asked if the Second Amendment should be up for reinterpretation, Foster said, "It always has been up for reinterpretation. The technology changes, and the weapons thought to be too dangerous to be in private hands change. A Civil War cannon is frankly much less dangerous than weapons we are allowed to carry on the streets in many of the states and cities in our country today. This is something where technology changes and public attitude changes and both are important in each of the generations."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/naperville-sun/ct-nvs-foster-gun-violence-forum-st-0404-20180403-story.html|title=Rep. Bill Foster: Second Amendment meant to be reinterpreted by each generation|last=Hegarty|first=Erin|website=Chicago Tribune |date=April 3, 2018 |access-date=2020-04-23|archive-date=2020-08-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806133640/https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/naperville-sun/ct-nvs-foster-gun-violence-forum-st-0404-20180403-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Israel-Palestine===
Foster voted to provide [[Israel]] with support following [[October 7 attacks]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Demirjian |first=Karoun |date=2023-10-25 |title=House Declares Solidarity With Israel in First Legislation Under New Speaker |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/10/25/us/politics/house-israel-vote.html |access-date=2023-10-30 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-25 |title=Roll Call 528 Roll Call 528, Bill Number: H. Res. 771, 118th Congress, 1st Session |url=https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2023528 |access-date=2023-10-30 |website=Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives |language=en}}</ref> On December 29, 2025, he cosponsored the West Bank Violence Prevention Act of 2025, which opposes Israeli violence in the West Bank.<ref>{{cite web |title=H.R.3045 - West Bank Violence Prevention Act of 2025 |url=https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3045/cosponsors |website=Congress.gov}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Foster and his wife, Aesook Byon, live in [[Naperville, Illinois]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/sleuth/2009/01/three_house_members_wearing_ne.html |newspaper=The Washington Post |title=Three House Members Wearing New Rings in the 111th |access-date=2013-02-08 |archive-date=2016-01-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160120222436/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/sleuth/2009/01/three_house_members_wearing_ne.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://query.nictusa.com/cgi-bin/dcdev/forms/C00435099/746348/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120717042556/http://query.nictusa.com/cgi-bin/dcdev/forms/C00435099/746348/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-17 |title=Foster, Bill – Statement of Candidacy |publisher=Federal Elections Commission |date=2011-09-29 |access-date=2011-10-04 }}</ref> He has two adult children from his first marriage to Ann Foster.<ref name="chitribmay" /> When Bill and Ann Foster divorced in the mid-nineties, they remained on good terms and agreed to live within blocks of each other. Their children lived at both of their houses. Foster is a grandparent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bill's Family |url=https://www.billfoster.com/meet-bill/bills-family/ |access-date=2023-12-10 |website=Bill Foster for Congress |language=en-US}}</ref>

Foster is among the few U.S. representatives not to identify with any religion.<ref name=pewforum>{{cite web|url=https://www.pewresearch.org/religion/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2022/12/PF_2023.01.03_congress_LIST.pdf|title=Religious affiliation of members of 118th Congress|publisher=Pew Research Center|date=January 3, 2023}}</ref>
